body.x: AVING News selected ▲Coway’s “AIRMEGA”, ▲Withings’ “Thermo”, ▲GOQUAL’s “BlueSwitch”, ▲Netatmo’s “Presence”, and ▲Roost’s “Roost” as the top five smart home products that were showcased at “CES 2016 (Consumer Technology Show)”, the world’s largest IT electronics and tech exhibition, which ran for four days from Wednesday the 6th to Saturday the 9th in Las Vegas.

The smart air purifier “AIRMEGA” measures indoor air quality by using an internal pollution sensor, creating a more comfortable breathing environment. Its mobile app sends real-time notifications and gives users the freedom to control the product anywhere, anytime. In particular, when users use the smart mode, it automatically adapts to its surroundings. It controls the fan speed based on air quality and lighting conditions.

Honored with the “CES 2016 Innovative Award”, the smart thermometer “Thermo” can measure body temperatures conveniently, quickly, and accurately, all by using its 16 IR sensors. It is connected to a smartphone via its app, and it enables users to save data to their smartphones in real time. Furthermore, it can track family members’ temperature records and send users’ data to doctors.

This is a Wi-Fi-based smart light control switch that can be easily installed on any building without additional equipment. It can turn on and off the light without a smartphone. This is achieved by using a remote control. It enables users to conveniently control the light without using the app. It can control up to three lighting products, and with the app, it can control a maximum 10 switches. It possesses alarm and timer functions, and has an eco mode that activates the power-saving mode when not in use. It can remotely control lights, automatically turn them on/off at set times, and save money on electricity bills.

Unlike existing security cameras, the “CES 2016 Innovative Award”-winning smart outdoor security camera “Presence” provides accurate information by recognizing cars, people, and animals. Based on such information, it can send notifications if there is a person, a car, or an animal sought by the user. By switching its function, it can be used as a night floodlight and a warning light for house break-ins. Furthermore, users can check real time or recorded videos, and the lights can be turned on/off via a remote control function.

This is a smart battery that can send alerts to smartphones when there is low battery for fire alarms or when alarms detect smoke. It can also notify family members and neighbors if users are not at home, or if they cannot move during an emergency situation like a fire. Users are also notified when the fire alarm has low battery.

“CES”, which is held every year in January by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is the world’s largest IT consumer electronics exhibition, showcasing global trends in the electronics and IT industry. AVING News, which has sent reporters to CES for 11 years, will introduce various up-to-date technologies and products showcased at CES 2016.
